history.summary: Kakanmath is a ruined 11th-century Shiva temple at Sihoniya (ancient Simhapaniya), Morena district, Madhya Pradesh (the CSV 'state' column holds the town name 'Morena' - the real state is Madhya Pradesh; the actual site is the village Sihoniya, ~65 km north of Gwalior). Built by the Kachchhapaghata ruler Kirttiraja (an inscription at the Sas-Bahu temple, Gwalior, records a Shiva temple built by him at Simhapaniya); tradition says it was raised for his queen Kakanwati, from whom the name may derive (alt. theory: Kanak, 'gold' + matha, 'shrine'). The original complex had a central temple with four subsidiary shrines; only part of the central two-storey structure survives, its sikhara stripped to ~30 m. It is famous for dry-stone construction with no mortar or cement, and for the folk legend that Shiva's ganas built it overnight and fled at dawn leaving it 'unfinished'. It is an ASI Monument of National Importance. Height estimates vary (100-130 ft); the ~30 m figure is from a site study. Some sculptures from the site are now in the Gwalior archaeological museum.

town_description: Sihoniya (also spelled Suhania) is a village in Morena district, Madhya Pradesh, once the capital of the Kachchhapaghata/Kushwaha kingdom in the early 11th century. The Kakanmath temple rises over fields in the village interior, about 65 km north of Gwalior; the site is an ASI-protected monument.
